customer_question: Our chipset reports Enhanced Power Control as supported when queried over HCI, but the InterLab RF Test System's certification test shows the DUT responding 'Not Supported' and aborts the RF/TRM/CA Enhanced Power Control test item. Why is there a discrepancy, and how should we get this resolved?
question_variants: Why does our HCI interface say EPC is supported but the certification test disagrees?
Does Enhanced Power Control need the peer device to support it too, and is that why our test failed?
How does the certification tester actually check Enhanced Power Control support during the RF/TRM/CA test?
What should we ask the chipset vendor to resolve this discrepancy?
actual_issue: A DUT's HCI command interface reported Enhanced Power Control (EPC) as supported, but during the actual InterLab RF Test System certification test, the DUT responded 'Not Supported' to the test system's initial support-check command sent over the air, causing the RF/TRM/CA Enhanced Power Control test item to be aborted -- creating an apparent contradiction between the HCI-reported capability and the DUT's behavior under the certification test's DUT mode.
plain_english_explanation: A chip can report that it supports a feature when asked directly through its command interface, but that's not necessarily what it actually does when a certification lab's automated test puts it into a special test mode and asks the same question over the air as part of the test. Here, the chip said 'yes' to the direct command-line question but said 'no' during the actual radio test, so the test that checks the feature couldn't proceed. This kind of mismatch is something only the chip's own vendor can really explain, so the right move is to hand them the exact log showing both answers and ask them to reconcile it.
consultant_answer: Bluetooth SIG certification RF testing is performed automatically by an SIG-certified test system (InterLab RF Test System in this case): test items are pre-selected from a menu, and the system sends test-control commands to the DUT via the antenna signal measurement port in sequence, executing each test item's spec-defined procedure. Each test item appears to begin with a command that checks feature support, and per the attached 2402MHz log (2441MHz and 2480MHz logs are the same content), the DUT responded 'Not Supported' to the RF test system over the antenna signal measurement terminal, logged as 'BT: ERROR: OUT indicates that it does not support Enhanced Power Control (EPC)' with an associated Final Verdict. Separately, for EPC to actually activate in real device-to-device operation, both devices in the connection must support it -- if the customer was checking whether EPC became active using a real peer device, the peer device's own EPC support should be confirmed; in real-device pairing, RF-layer negotiation only activates capabilities both sides commonly support. The certification tester, however, does support the RF/TRM/CA (Enhanced Power Control) test item directly: if pre-selected, the test stage sends Power Up/Power Down commands to the DUT per the EPC specification. In this case, because the DUT under DUT mode itself responded 'Not support Enhanced Power Control,' the RF Test System aborted that test item at that point, independent of any peer-device consideration. The recommended next step is to ask the chipset vendor directly: report that the HCI command interface shows Enhanced Power Control as supported (YES), but the InterLab RF Test System's test log shows 'ERROR: OUT indicates that it does not support Enhanced Power Control,' causing the RF/TRM/CA (Enhanced Power Control) test item to not pass, and request the vendor's advice on how to address it.
decision_logic: When a DUT's HCI-reported feature support disagrees with its behavior during an actual certification test item, the certification test's own support-check response -- sent and received over the air while the DUT is in DUT mode -- is the operative signal for whether that specific test item can proceed, regardless of what the HCI interface separately reports; this is distinct from the question of whether the feature would activate during real device-to-device negotiation, which depends on both peer devices' support and does not explain a single-DUT certification test abort.
final_recommendation: Do not assume the HCI-reported support status settles whether the RF/TRM/CA Enhanced Power Control test item will pass. Escalate the specific contradiction to the chipset vendor with the exact log evidence (HCI says supported; RF Test System logs 'does not support Enhanced Power Control') and request their guidance on resolving the DUT-mode behavior before reattempting the test item.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming the feature is properly supported based on the HCI-level report alone, without escalating the DUT-mode behavior discrepancy to the chipset vendor, risks repeated failure of the RF/TRM/CA Enhanced Power Control test item without identifying or fixing the underlying cause.
